query: For high-entropy-alloy protective coatings in wear-resistant applications, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs their wear performance and why? Define a controlled change that would distinguish the hypothesis from a baseline, the directional observations expected if it is correct, the range over which it should hold, the prior evidence that supports it, and an observation that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: In nanocrystalline high-entropy alloy (HEA) wear-protective coatings, the specific wear rate is governed primarily by the magnitude of the average atomic-size-mismatch parameter (δ); coatings whose δ exceeds ~5 % form a harder, distortion-stabilised solid solution that suppresses dislocation activity and grain-boundary sliding, thereby lowering wear by at least 30 % compared with otherwise similar coatings having δ ≤ 3 %.
generation.material_initial_state: As-deposited 3–5 µm thick equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA coating on hardened tool steel, nanocrystalline (~20 nm) f.c.c. solid solution, no secondary phases.
generation.intervention: Modify the alloy to CoCrFeMnNi₀.₈Al₀.₂ (adds smaller Al atoms, reducing δ from ≈4.8 % to ≈3.0 %) while keeping grain size, thickness, substrate, and deposition parameters constant.
generation.conditions: Room-temperature unlubricated pin-on-disk test, 10 N normal load, 0.1 m s⁻¹ sliding speed, ambient lab air (≈45 % RH).
generation.structural_mediator: Average atomic-size mismatch parameter δ acts through lattice distortion that raises solid-solution hardening and decreases dislocation mean free path, increasing coating hardness (H) and H/E* ratio.
generation.mechanism: Greater lattice distortion (>5 %) increases Peierls barrier and impedes dislocation glide, maintaining high hardness during sliding; reduced plasticity delays debris formation and crack nucleation, yielding lower wear.
generation.predicted_outcome: The modified low-δ coating will show ≥30 % higher specific wear rate (mm³ N⁻¹ m⁻¹) and ≥15 % lower nano-indentation hardness relative to the baseline high-δ coating under the stated conditions.
generation.baseline: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi coating with δ≈4.8 %, measured specific wear rate W₀ and hardness H₀.
generation.boundary: Effect expected for nanocrystalline single-phase f.c.c. HEA coatings with 3 % < δ < 8 %, grain size <50 nm, tested at 20–150 °C in mild oxidative ambient. Outside this range (coarse grains, multiphase alloys, lubricated contact, or temperatures where oxidation dominates) other mechanisms may govern wear.
generation.uncertainty: δ threshold (≈5 %) and exact % change in wear may vary with grain size and testing temperature; lack of prior systematic δ-controlled studies adds moderate uncertainty.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two coatings: (A) baseline CoCrFeMnNi (δ≈4.8 %) and (B) modified CoCrFeMnNi₀.₈Al₀.₂ (δ≈3.0 %), with matched thickness and grain size. Conduct triplicate pin-on-disk tests under the stated conditions, measure wear track volume by 3D profilometry and hardness by nano-indentation pre- and post-test.
measurements: Specific wear rate W (mm³ N⁻¹ m⁻¹)
Nano-indentation hardness H and elastic modulus E*
Post-wear cross-sectional TEM for dislocation density and grain size
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If coating B (lower δ) shows (i) specific wear rate ≤ 10 % higher than or equal to coating A, and/or (ii) hardness within ±5 % of coating A despite its lower δ, the hypothesis is falsified.
